S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving a battery, including overheating, smoke, or fire, to the relevant regulator within 5 business days of learning of it, even if there is no injury or property damage. Incidents involving death, serious injury, active fire, evacuation, or an ongoing danger to the public must be reported within 24 hours. ... Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident presents a credible safety risk requiring immediate precautions; otherwise, include relevant safety information in the next customer communication.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and after a material design or manufacturing change. ... Each customer who buys a model must receive that model’s precise per-model failure rate and test results, alongside safety explanations, precautions, and corrective actions. Identifiable per-model results must not be published to the general public. ... no single test failure-rate threshold automatically bars a model from market.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market must support secure remote emergency shut-off... Manufacturers must provide a retrofit plan for installed units and complete retrofits within 6 years of this standard taking effect, prioritizing units presenting the greatest safety risk. Where retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the owner and regulator and provide an alternative risk-reduction measure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. The requirement applies to units manufactured on or after that date. Regulators should specify performance and maintenance criteria and may approve an equivalent protective design where it provides comparable risk reduction.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Below that threshold, regulators may require corrective action, customer notice, or a recall based on the nature and severity of the risk. Manufacturers must promptly notify regulators and affected customers of a recall and provide clear remedy instructions.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict and safe, requiring reporting of all incidents and prompt customer notice. S2 is weakened: no permanent failure-rate cap, so Hearth 10 is not barred, but customers receive precise per-model rates and public disclosure is barred. S3 and S4 are acceptable compromises (6-year retrofit, 36-month suppression), while S5 is weakened with a 10/100k recall trigger that spares Ember 8.
